name: jev-gate
description: Use when a jev answer decides whether a command runs, a step continues, a build fails or a low confidence answer goes to a human, and before writing 'if jev', 'jev ... && cmd', -q or --assert. Two common gate recipes look right and are silently wrong.
compatibility: Requires the jev binary on PATH.

rules.short: Phrase the question so that true means go, not stop.
rules.why: Under `-q` the exit code tracks the answer, not safety. A question phrased in the danger direction exits 0 when the answer is true, so a script written as `jev ... && eval "$cmd"` runs the dangerous input and blocks the safe one. Measured: 'is this command destructive' with `--threshold 0.5` exits 0 for 'rm -rf ./build' and 1 for 'ls -la'.
rules.good: jev 'is this command safe to run' -q --threshold 0.5 --state 'rm -rf ./build'

rules.short: Never add -q to --assert. Redirect stdout instead.
rules.why: `-q` adds its own 0.5 gate and both must pass. A safety assert like `value < 0.5` is true exactly when that gate is false, so the pair never passes. `--assert` alone already sets the exit code.

rules.short: Treat every non zero exit as no, not just exit 1.
rules.why: Exit 1 means the policy said no. Exits 2 through 5 mean no answer arrived at all, from a usage error, a bad key, an exhausted retry or a transport failure. Exit 6 means a stream finished with at least one failed record, so a gate over a stream still has to fail closed on it. Chaining with `&&` fails closed on all of them as a minimal gate, which is correct. Branching on exit 1 alone treats an outage and a typo as an answer. To tell them apart: `case $? in 0) go ;; 1) block ;; *) alert and block ;; esac`.
rules.bad: jev ... --assert '...' --state "$cmd"; if [ $? -eq 1 ]; then block; else eval "$cmd"; fi

rules.short: -q gates one question on one record. Use --assert for several questions or a stream.
rules.why: jev rejects `-q` outright when more than one question was asked, naming them, and under any streaming input mode, since an exit code cannot carry more than one answer. A gate over several questions or a stream instead uses `--assert`, which prints every record and exits 1 when any assertion was false.
rules.bad_unverifiable: the checker strips -q before every dry run, so it cannot observe this rejection
rules.good: jev --ask a='destroys data' --ask b='sends credentials' --assert 'a.value < 0.5 and b.value < 0.5' --state 'rm -rf ./build'

rules.short: Gate a pick or rate on --min-confidence and give --fallback a human routed value.
rules.why: `--min-confidence` needs `--fallback`. Below the threshold the decision becomes the fallback text instead of the model's pick, and `.fallback` reads `low_confidence`, so a consumer routes on that field rather than trusting a low confidence guess.
rules.bad: jev --ask team='which team owns this incident' --pick billing,shipping,support --min-confidence 0.7 --state 'the payment silently failed at checkout'
rules.good: jev --ask team='which team owns this incident' --pick billing,shipping,support --min-confidence 0.99 --fallback human --state 'the tracking number in the shipping confirmation email matches a charge that appears twice on the invoice'

rules.short: Check an assertion with --print-questions before you spend anything.
rules.why: `--print-questions` writes the assertion into the file it prints and checks every path and type against the questions, so a typo or a type error exits 2 naming the real question ids and makes no network call. The good example below keeps the typo on purpose, so it exits 2 naming the real id `urgent` rather than running for real. `--print-request` rejects `--assert`, so use `--print-questions`.

rules.short: Do the arithmetic in jq, not in --assert.
rules.why: The assertion language compares and combines. It does not add, multiply or weight. Weighting several answers is the consumer's job, so print the record and let `jq` do it, as in `jev --ask urgency='how urgent is this' --ask anger='how angry is the writer' --state "$t" -o values | jq '(.urgency.value * 2 + .anger.value) / 3'`.
rules.good: jev --ask urgency='how urgent is this' --ask anger='how angry is the writer' --state "$t" -o values | jq '(.urgency.value * 2 + .anger.value) / 3'

rules.short: Write an id with a space, dot or hyphen as ["my id"].value.
rules.why: A question id or an option label containing a dot, a space or a hyphen cannot be written with a plain dot path. The id comes first and still needs its field after it.
